units.passage: Use of these tools, or other similar generative AI tools, will not be tolerated and will be considered plagiarism and could result in the student failing the course.
units.policy: Use of these generative AI tools will be considered plagiarism.

units.passage: If AI misuse is confirmed, enforce the academic integrity policies accordingly.

units.passage: Work authored by another (including material created by ChatGPT and other Generative AI tools) but represented as the student’s work, whether paraphrased or copied verbatim or in near-verbatim form, is considered plagiarism.
units.policy: Work authored by another, including material created by ChatGPT and other Generative AI tools, but represented as the student's work, whether paraphrased or copied verbatim or in near-verbatim form, is considered plagiarism.

units.passage: University policy states that work authored by another (including material created by ChatGPT and other Generative AI tools) but represented as the student’s work, whether paraphrased or copied verbatim or in near-verbatim form, is considered plagiarism.

units.passage: Violation of this Policy may be classified as serious misconduct, which is grounds for discipline in accordance with the Faculty Handbook, staff employment policies, and the Student Handbook as appropriate. Any disciplinary action under this Policy will consider the severity of the offense and the individual’s intent and could include termination of access to the USC network, USC systems, software, and/or applications, as well as employment actions up to and including termination.
units.why: 'Violation of this Policy may be classified as serious misconduct, which is grounds for discipline' under faculty, staff and student rules: P36 with a fit note because this is a general policy, not coursework integrity.
units.fit_note: Covers employees and students under this policy, with sanctions up to termination, not only academic misconduct. | Misconduct here is violating the IT policy on tools and data, not academic dishonesty; it also lists sanctions (P37).

units.passage: the committee recommends that instructors remind students that the acquisition of academic work in whole or in part from any source (from textbooks and journal articles to web resources to generative AI) and the subsequent presentation of those materials as the student's own work (whether that material is paraphrased or copied in verbatim or near-verbatim form) constitutes an academic integrity violation unless otherwise allowed by the instructor.
units.policy: Instructors should remind students that acquiring academic work in whole or in part from any source, including generative AI, and presenting it as their own constitutes an academic integrity violation unless otherwise allowed by the instructor.
units.why: Instructors should remind students that presenting work from 'any source (from textbooks and journal articles to web resources to generative AI)' as their own 'constitutes an academic integrity violation unless otherwise allowed by the instructor'. The operative rule is that unauthorized use is a violation unless the instructor allows it, so P36; the any-source framing (P45) is recorded as a fit n
units.fit_note: Also treats generative AI like textbooks and web sources under one rule. | Treats AI as a source under integrity rules; it is not about AI as a collaborator.

units.passage: While each school maintains its own system, evidentiary standards, and procedures for identifying and adjudicating cases of academic misconduct, the College and each school should ensure that existing processes and criteria in judicial frameworks and academic honor codes are adequate to address academic misconduct with GAI.
units.policy: The College and each school should ensure that existing processes and criteria in judicial frameworks and academic honor codes are adequate to address academic misconduct with GAI.
units.why: Directs schools to check that honor codes and judicial frameworks can 'address academic misconduct with GAI', bringing AI misuse under integrity processes (P36).
units.fit_note: Directs units to update integrity processes; does not itself classify AI misuse as misconduct. | Directs schools to adapt honor codes so GAI misconduct can be handled; does not itself classify misuse

units.passage: For example: “The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student, whether in the classroom, laboratory, studio, intern- and externships, independent research settings, or other spaces identified as serving educational goals.”
units.policy: Honor codes and judicial standards clearly state the definition of academic misconduct relative to GAI; an example definition is 'The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student, whether in the classroom, laboratory, studio, intern- and externships, independent research settings, or other spaces identified as serving educational goals.'
units.why: Under the heading 'Clearly state the definition of Academic Misconduct relative to GAI', the page recommends that honor codes define misconduct as GAI use 'without permission' and offers the example 'The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student'. It recommends a definition (P36 over P61, which defines AI rather than misuse). The example makes unauthorized use misconduct, so GAI use

units.passage: GAI may impact learning contexts and assessments in ways that require new structures for producing authentic student work that are distinct from those described in existing honor codes and definitions.
units.policy: GAI may impact learning contexts and assessments in ways that require new structures for producing authentic student work that are distinct from those described in existing honor codes and definitions.

units.fit_note: Explains why definitions need updating; does not itself classify misuse

units.passage: Academic misconduct includes but is not limited to cheating, plagiarism (including unauthorized use of artificial intelligence), fabrication or falsification of data or records, unauthorized copying or collaboration, resume or credential falsification, unauthorized use of resources, violation of test-taking conditions, or otherwise engaging in activity prohibited by the University or Academic Integrity policy.
units.why: The opening sentence classes 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as plagiarism and so as academic misconduct, which is the integrity-process classification (P36), not a stance rule.

units.passage: NOTE: It is important to remember that the unauthorized use of generative AI in a course is a violation of WSU’s Community Standards and can be reported to the Center for Community Standards (CCS).
units.why: "the unauthorized use of generative AI in a course is a violation of WSU's Community Standards" classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36). It does not command, so informs; it forbids only use without authorization, so unit_stance restrict.

units.passage: AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism.
units.why: The same example says such submissions "will be treated as plagiarism", which classes misuse as plagiarism, so P36.

units.passage: But there will be instances when some students might misuse AI or otherwise go against explicit instructions to not use AI.
units.why: "some students might misuse AI or otherwise go against explicit instructions to not use AI" notes misuse can occur where an instructor bans AI; informational P36.
units.fit_note: Does not classify misuse formally; acknowledges it can happen.

units.passage: We have noted concerns from faculty about academic misconduct issues with AI, about syllabus policies, concerns that are shared by formal committees in departments, units, or divisions that have provided guidance to faculty on AI and teaching, and on the various uses of AI by faculty for teaching purposes.

units.fit_note: Notes faculty concern about misconduct; does not itself classify AI misuse as misconduct.

It states a classification rather than giving a separate command, so modality is informs, and since AI stays allowed with permission the unit stance is restrict.

units.passage: This includes words, ideas, and images generated by artificial intelligence.
